scenes.headline: How an image editor learns to see depth
scenes.sub: Marigold V2: a frozen 4-bit diffusion transformer, a thin LoRA, one pass.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Noodles! Marigold V2 turns a twenty billion parameter image-editing model into a depth estimator. Here's how.

scenes.label: The recipe
scenes.text: An image generator already knows scene geometry. Freeze one at 4-bit, train a thin LoRA, and read depth off one forward pass.
scenes.say: The bet: an image generator already knows geometry. Freeze one at four bits, train a thin adapter, and read depth off a single pass.

scenes.title: Photo in, depth out, one pass

steps.say: The photo is encoded to a latent. The frozen transformer, twenty billion weights at four bits, reads it at one fixed timestep, point five.
Only a rank one twenty-eight LoRA adapter trains: about eight hundred fifty-two million parameters, four point two percent of the transformer.
It predicts a velocity. Subtract that from the photo's latent, decode, and you have depth. One pass, no sampling loop.

scenes.title: Two stages on one 32 GB GPU

items.say: Stage one trains the adapter with iREPA, which aligns its hidden states with DINOv3 features of the true depth map, not the photo.
Stage two adds SinkLoss and unfreezes the VAE decoder, for about one more day.

left.title: Plain per-pixel L1
items: Pixel i must match pixel i
Noisy edges teach the model to hedge
left.say: A plain loss makes each pixel match its exact twin. At noisy synthetic edges, that teaches the model to hedge and blur.

right.title: SinkLoss
items: Match the 25 values in each 5x5 block
A soft one-to-one assignment, by optimal transport
right.say: SinkLoss asks each five by five block only for the same depth values, matched by optimal transport. An edge off by a pixel costs almost nothing.

scenes.title: AbsRel gain over the previous best, by benchmark
scenes.note: the abstract quotes the best two; the five-way average is 12.1%
scenes.say: Best in its data class on all five benchmarks. The quoted sixteen to twenty-six percent are the top two; the average is twelve point one.

scenes.text: A generative prior plus the right losses makes a sharp depth model: align to the target, and match values, not pixels.
scenes.say: Align to the target, and match values, not pixels: that's what turns a generative prior into a sharp depth model.

recap: A frozen 4-bit DiT, adapted by a rank-128 LoRA
Fixed timestep: depth in one forward pass
iREPA and SinkLoss keep fine structure sharp
scenes.say: To recap: a frozen transformer, a thin adapter, one pass, and two losses for sharp edges.
